chunks: His companion will say: 'O Lord, I did not lead him to wickedness, but he was himself far astray.'

key_terms.قَرِينُهُ: his companion (referring to the shaytan or angel)

ai.seo_question: What does the shaytan say to God on the Day of Judgment regarding his companion?
ai.summary: In this verse from Surah Qaf, the shaytan (devil) testifies against his human charge, denying that he forced the individual into sin but rather that the person chose a 'far error' through their own free will. Shia scholars highlight this as a key moment of accountability where the external tempter shifts blame to the internal choice of the human, emphasizing that while the shaytan provides the whisper, the human retains the agency to accept or reject it.
